title: Minimum Interventions Exposing Disagreement between d-Separation and Sigma-Separation

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the external-parent-boundary characterization, explicit falsifying witness, universal-apex recurrence, sharp exposure range, paired-arborescence certificate, and an endpoint-selecting bounded-treewidth dynamic program. A final targeted repair made the compact decomposition input explicit, closing the sole mathematical-review finding. The package was downgraded because the delivered result remains a known-graph regime-wise diagnostic and lacks the reference implementation, end-to-end oracle validation, practical constants, and broader testing or pooled-data consequences needed to clear the field floor.
tldr: How many fixed hard-intervention targets are needed before d-separation and sigma-separation disagree in a known finite directed mixed graph? The note proves that this minimum is the smallest external-parent boundary of an induced set whose SCC completion creates a new district-family moral edge. The proof returns an optimal intervention and explicit conditional-independence witness, yields the universal-apex recurrence and every finite exposure through \(n-4\), and supports a sound-complete endpoint-selecting four-partition dynamic program running in \(2^{O(t\log(t+2))}n\) time on original-skeleton treewidth \(t\). The only unresolved deliverables are the reference implementation, its end-to-end oracle tests, and measured practical constants. Statistical conclusions remain regime-wise under all-principal regularity and d-Markovness, with no pooled-JCI faithfulness claim.
gap: Forré--Mooij provide the moralization and SCC-completion machinery for comparing d- and sigma-separation, but the inspected literature does not quantify the minimum intervention needed to expose their difference, recover an optimal CI witness, characterize the extremal values, or optimize the quantity on bounded-treewidth skeletons.
fill: Prove the external-parent-boundary identity and structural consequences, then establish and implement a sparse paired-arborescence certificate and explicit nice-tree-decomposition optimizer. Use the exact exponential solver as an oracle for a preregistered transition-level validation, and state causal conclusions only for each fixed postintervention regime.
